# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b40 — Coordinated PID outputs and measured-model calibration

## Why this beta

PID previously time-proportioned every binary-capable primary fan regardless of whether it also supported continuous speed modulation. Percentage fans could therefore receive both duty-cycle and speed modulation. Discrete Low/Medium/High native fan speeds followed selected profiles, but were not mapped to their device's heating/drying/air PID demand. Quiet-room speed caps worked independently.

This release coordinates **one per-device PID demand** across the exact capabilities already advertised by the selected physical device. It does not merge independently selected physical devices into one unsafe group or invent native services.

## Physical outputs

- **Pure ON/OFF**: retain safe, slow duty-cycle PWM and the physical source's minimum ON/OFF, maximum runtime, ownership and acknowledgement checks.
- **0–100% direct number valve/output**: retain gradual native output modulation (≤10 percentage points per update), rather than also duty cycling the same demand.
- **Standalone proportional fan**: modulate actual supported fan percentage from PID demand, instead of applying a second PWM fraction. Below the physical minimum fan speed, remain OFF; power transitions still require native hardware permission and dwell checks.
- **Native ordered discrete fan**: recognize only real advertised Low/Medium/High or numbered level series, then map PID demand to one of those real stages. For unrecognized presets like Auto/Natural, preserve user-selected normal/profile mode instead of making up an order.
- **Combined climate or drying device with a native fan**: the heating/drying duty cycle remains the primary actuator, but its fan speed can additionally follow the same computed demand while the native device is running.
- **Quiet rooms**: the existing per-device Quiet when sleeping / Quiet when occupied switches cap percentage or discrete fan speed to the configured quiet percentage/native stage. Uncertain sleep/occupancy evidence prevents raising fan speeds and prevents starting a quiet-configured device into an unknown quiet context. Quiet does not silently modify a heater/valve target or bypass thermal protection.

All modulation is limited to explicitly selected same-area devices and existing physical capabilities. Native power is never turned on merely to change fan speed.

## Per-device deterministic PID calibration

A new per-device **PID calibration method** selector is available when the controller's **Control method is PID**:

1. **Manual** — existing editable Kp, Ki and Kd; no automatic changes, default for all existing installs.
2. **IMC / Lambda (Skogestad SIMC PI)** — conservative measured first-order-plus-dead-time model; computes PI gains with Kd=0.
3. **Cohen–Coon (reaction-curve PID)** — an inherently more aggressive measured open-loop reaction-curve formula; appropriate only for a genuine identified self-regulating process.

For model-based methods the operator enters the *measured* process gain (change in physical measured variable per full 0→100% actuator step), process time constant, dead time, and Lambda target response time (IMC only), all from an actual step-response identification. The model must be slower than the controller sample interval and the computed parallel-form gains must fall **within the existing Kp/Ki/Kd hardware bounds**. No guessed coefficients or silent clipping.

The new **Apply PID calibration** button previews calculation status, then applies the proposed gains only after an explicit press while the exact physical output is truly **OFF** with no active owned power or pending acknowledgement. The code makes **no relay experiment, induced oscillation, actuator power/service request or synthetic test pulse**. Source identity stays associated with the stored calibration record. Editing model fields alone never changes active PID gains. Manual Kp/Ki/Kd and all previously selected modes stay untouched on invalid model data.

These are deterministic *formula-based model tuners*, not one-click autonomous system identification. No real physical step measurements can be safely inferred from device names or current sensor readings.

Reference methods: [Skogestad SIMC / IMC PI](https://www.isa.org/intech-home/2016/may-june/departments/loop-tuning-basics-self-regulating-processes) and [Cohen–Coon (NI)](https://www.ni.com/docs/en-US/bundle/labview/page/cohen-coon-autotuning-method.html). Both require the process model; controller form is converted to parallel Kp, Ki=Kp/Ti, Kd=Kp·Td, with time in minutes matching the current PID implementation.

## Availability and controls

Per-device calibration method (select), four measured-model parameters (number), apply button, and read-only calibration/output strategy diagnostics are available on the controller device. The room dashboard also displays the method selector, model inputs and explicit Apply action when PID is active. All actions are scoped to matching physical-source IDs; user-initiated Save does not itself apply a tune.

## Preserved software safety

No device- or brand-specific branches, no legacy domain, no migration, and no physical actuator commissioning on install. Native device minimum ON/OFF, max ON, window, selected room, feedback freshness, occupancy/sleep, defrosting, pending acknowledgment, source-device identity, and manual intervention remain enforced. Independent logical control channels still do not override one another.

Beta31–39 features remain included. Stable Latest remains v0.5.1. Publish only after complete Python 3.13/3.14, HA 2026.10, frontend, 38-language catalog, HACS/Hassfest and canonical flat-tag verification.
